section: Evolution of Panchayati Raj - Community Development Programme, Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, G.V.K. Rao and L.M. Singhvi committees

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the constitutional evolution of Panchayati Raj in India?
o: It moved directly from municipal administration to Part IX of the Constitution
It originated exclusively from the recommendations of the Finance Commission
It evolved from development schemes such as the Community Development Programme to self-government under justiciable Part IX
It developed from urban local bodies and was later included in the Directive Principles of State Policy
accepted.x: Panchayati Raj evolved from rural development schemes, particularly the Community Development Programme, towards constitutionalised local self-government under Part IX. Article 40 in the Directive Principles provided an earlier constitutional basis.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that captures the complete institutional evolution rather than a partial stage.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the recent reorganisation of Panchayati Raj institutions in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The erstwhile 13 Zilla Praja Parishads have been reorganised into 28 Zilla Praja Parishads.
2. The current terms of the Mandal Praja Parishads end on 23 September 2026.
3. The current terms of the Zilla Praja Parishads end on 24 September 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh has reorganised its former 13 Zilla Praja Parishads into 28, while the MPP and ZPP terms end on 23 and 24 September 2026 respectively.
accepted.tq: Verify each current numerical and date-based statement independently.

accepted.s: In the Panchayati Raj structure of Andhra Pradesh, which institution occupies the intermediate tier?
o: District Rural Council
Firka Development Committee
Mandal Praja Parishad
Block Panchayat Samiti
accepted.x: The distinctive intermediate-level institution in Andhra Pradesh is the Mandal Praja Parishad. It is not called a block Panchayat Samiti as in the conventional model.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the general block-level terminology and the Andhra Pradesh-specific institution.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages in the historical evolution of Panchayati Raj in the correct chronological order:
A. Acceptance of the Balwant Rai Mehta model by the National Development Council
B. Launch of the Community Development Programme
C. Implementation of Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh
D. Launch of the National Extension Service
o: B, D, A, C
D, B, A, C
B, A, D, C
D, A, B, C
accepted.x: The sequence was Community Development Programme, National Extension Service, National Development Council acceptance in January 1958, and implementation in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh in 1959.
accepted.tq: Use the development-scheme-to-institution sequence and place the NDC decision before the 1959 implementation.

accepted.s: The Community Development Programme is significant in the evolution of Indian local governance because it was:
o: A programme exclusively designed for tribal self-government
The first urban poverty alleviation programme after Independence
India's first constitutional amendment concerning local bodies
India's first major post-Independence rural development programme
accepted.x: The Community Development Programme was India's first major post-Independence rural development programme and laid the groundwork for a third tier of government.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise historical status of the programme rather than its later constitutional consequence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the implementation of the Balwant Rai Mehta model in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: It was implemented on 2 October 1959 under the government of N. Sanjiva Reddy
It was implemented on 1 November 1959 under the government of N. Sanjiva Reddy
It was implemented in 1978 under the government of Jalagam Vengala Rao
It was implemented in 1992 after the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh implemented the three-tier Balwant Rai Mehta model on 1 November 1959 under Chief Minister N. Sanjiva Reddy's government.
accepted.tq: Separate the Andhra Pradesh implementation date from the commonly associated Rajasthan date.

accepted.s: The first elections to Zilla Parishads, Samithis and Panchayats in Andhra Pradesh were notable for:
o: Their postponement until after the 73rd Amendment
Village and caste clashes
The complete absence of social conflict
The exclusive participation of political parties
accepted.x: The first elections in Andhra Pradesh witnessed village and caste clashes, demonstrating the social tensions accompanying the introduction of local political institutions.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive consequence associated with the first elections rather than the institutional date.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares the recommendations concerning the role of the Collector in Panchayati Raj?
o: The ARC alone favoured a smaller role for the Collector
All the committees favoured a Collector-chaired Zilla Parishad
Balwant Rai Mehta favoured a Collector-chaired Zilla Parishad, whereas the ARC, Ashok Mehta and G.V.K. Rao favoured a smaller role for the Collector
Balwant Rai Mehta opposed the Collector's role, whereas Ashok Mehta strengthened it
accepted.x: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee favoured a Collector-chaired Zilla Parishad. The Administrative Reforms Commission, Ashok Mehta Committee and G.V.K. Rao Committee sought to reduce the Collector's role.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into the Balwant Rai Mehta position and the later committees' position.

accepted.s:
With reference to the recommendations concerning district planning, consider the following statements:
1. Hanumantha Rao and Dantwala kept the Collector central to district planning.
2. G.V.K. Rao recommended a District Development Council.
3. Hanumantha Rao retained the Collector as the main coordinator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. G.V.K. Rao wanted a District Development Committee (DDC), not a District Development Council; hence statement 2 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Watch for the wrong expansion of an institutional abbreviation in a comparison question.

accepted.s: The Firka Development Scheme, which covered areas corresponding to present-day Andhra Pradesh, was associated with:
o: The Hyderabad State in 1952
The Madras Presidency in 1946
The Government of India in 1973
The Andhra State in 1959
accepted.x: The Firka Development Scheme was introduced in the Madras Presidency in 1946 and covered areas that include present-day Andhra regions.
accepted.tq: Combine the location and year to distinguish the scheme from later nationwide programmes.

accepted.s: The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj (NIRDPR) is headquartered at:
o: New Delhi
Jaipur
Bengaluru
Hyderabad
accepted.x: NIRDPR, the national institute concerned with rural development and Panchayati Raj, is headquartered in Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use the location-specific institutional recall method.

accepted.s: Since 2016, the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) has supported approximately how many rural enterprises?
o: 1.32 lakh
2.48 lakh
4.32 lakh
8.64 lakh
accepted.x: SVEP has supported approximately 4.32 lakh rural enterprises since 2016.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact quantitative figure among closely spaced alternatives.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Ashok Mehta Committee is correct?
o: It rejected constitutional recognition and recommended only official nominations
It recommended abolition of all elected rural institutions
It confined its recommendations exclusively to municipal corporations
It was the first committee to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections for Panchayati Raj Institutions
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee was significant for being the first to seek constitutional recognition and party-based elections for Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Identify the committee through its distinctive recommendation rather than its appointment details.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the implementation history of the Ashok Mehta Committee's two-tier model?
o: It was adopted uniformly by all States
It was never adopted nationally
It was adopted nationally through the 73rd Amendment
It was adopted only in Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: The Ashok Mehta Committee's two-tier model was never adopted nationally. The 73rd Amendment subsequently retained a three-tier framework, subject to the population-based exception.
accepted.tq: Find the historically accurate exception to an apparently influential committee recommendation.

accepted.s: Under the constitutional framework introduced by the 73rd Amendment, a two-tier Panchayati Raj structure may exist in:
o: States with a population below 20 lakh
States with a population above 20 lakh only
All Union Territories irrespective of population
States with a population below 10 lakh only
accepted.x: The general constitutional model is three-tiered, but states with a population below 20 lakh may have only two tiers.
accepted.tq: Focus on the population threshold that creates the constitutional exception.

accepted.s: Which combination of committees is associated with the principal blueprint of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Balwant Rai Mehta, Hanumantha Rao and Dantwala
L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil
G.V.K. Rao, K. Santhanam and R.R. Diwakar
Ashok Mehta, S.D. Mishra and Rajagopalan
accepted.x: The L.M. Singhvi, Thungon and Gadgil Committees collectively contributed to the blueprint of the 73rd Amendment, including constitutional status, election and financial institutions, tenure and reservation.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive three-committee combination linked with constitutionalisation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding women’s representation in Panchayati Raj Institutions:
1. Women constitute more than 49.7 per cent of elected panchayat representatives.
2. Nineteen States and Union Territories reserve 50 per cent of seats for women.
3. The constitutional framework permits no reservation for women in Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because reservation for women is an important feature of Panchayati Raj institutions.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the established reservation principle.

accepted.s: The 17th National Panchayati Raj Day was observed on:
o: 24 April 2024
2 October 2026
24 April 2025
24 April 2026
accepted.x: The 17th National Panchayati Raj Day was held on 24 April 2026.
accepted.tq: Match the ordinal number with the corresponding year rather than relying only on the recurring date.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Panchayati Raj in West Bengal is correct?
o: The panchayat law was passed in 1959 and the first elections were held in 1960
The panchayat law was passed in 1973 and the first panchayat elections were held in June 1978
The panchayat law was passed in 1992 and the first elections were held in 1993
West Bengal has never conducted panchayat elections
accepted.x: West Bengal passed its panchayat Act in 1973 and conducted its first panchayat elections in June 1978.
accepted.tq: Link the enactment year with the later election year to eliminate reversed sequences.

accepted.s: The 2026 amendment in West Bengal concerning pradhans primarily:
o: Transferred all panchayat powers to municipalities
Introduced direct election of the Governor
Abolished the office of pradhan
Curbed the financial powers of pradhans
accepted.x: The 2026 amendment curtailed the financial powers of pradhans.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise subject of the amendment instead of assuming institutional abolition.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh has how many Mandal Praja Parishads according to the current administrative position?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has Mandal Praja Parishads for its 588 mandals.
accepted.tq: Use the exact administrative count and distinguish it from nearby numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Which Bill was the first attempt to provide constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Bill
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Bill
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Bill
The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill
accepted.x: The Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill was the first attempt to confer constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions. It failed in the Rajya Sabha in 1989.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first failed constitutional attempt from the later successful amendment.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 is correct?
o: It concerns the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha and was defeated in April 2026
It concerns Panchayati Raj reservations and has already become an Act
It concerns the abolition of the Rajya Sabha and was rejected in 1989
It concerns simultaneous elections and remains under consideration of a Joint Parliamentary Committee
accepted.x: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 concerns simultaneous elections and remains with a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two differently numbered constitutional bills and their subjects.

accepted.s: The parliamentary route followed by the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 is comparable to the route followed by the Panchayati Raj Bills of 1991 because both were:
o: Introduced only in State Legislatures
Referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee
Rejected by the Supreme Court before introduction
Passed without a special majority
accepted.x: Both matters followed the Joint Parliamentary Committee route. A Joint Parliamentary Committee is a parliamentary scrutiny mechanism and does not itself replace the constitutional requirement of a special majority.
accepted.tq: Identify the common parliamentary procedure rather than the substantive subject of the bills.

accepted.s: Why did the Constitution (64th Amendment) Bill fail to confer constitutional status on Panchayati Raj Institutions?
o: It was withdrawn by every State Legislature before introduction
It concerned only urban local bodies and was never debated
It was declared unconstitutional by the Election Commission
It was defeated in the Rajya Sabha in 1989 because the required special-majority route was not completed
accepted.x: The 64th Bill failed in the Rajya Sabha in 1989. A constitutional amendment requires the prescribed special majority, and failure at that stage prevented its enactment.
accepted.tq: Apply the special-majority requirement to explain why a constitutional bill failed.

accepted.s: Which development best explains the significance of the 1992 constitutional changes concerning Panchayati Raj?
o: They made Panchayati Raj Institutions justiciable and imposed a constitutional obligation on States
They transferred all rural development functions to the Union Government
They converted Panchayati Raj into a non-justiciable administrative experiment
They abolished the three-tier system throughout India
accepted.x: The 1992 constitutional changes transformed Panchayati Raj from a largely policy-based arrangement into a constitutionally protected and justiciable system, creating obligations for the States.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal consequence of constitutionalisation rather than merely its institutional form.
